The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a69fca6b458f542a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For V, p, E as above, choose either of the two pairs (d, H) = (1/32, 109 ) or (1/16, 108 ). (9) There is a smooth force on T3, effectively determined by V, p, for which zero initial velocity has a global smooth solution, unique in the classical torus class of Section 1, with pressure zero and the following properties. 1. If Ψk(p) ∈ E for some integer k ≥ 0, then u3(t, Y, z) > 1/2 for some finite t and some Y ∈ E. 2. If distT2 (Ψs(p), E) ≥ 2d for every s ≥ 0, then u3(t, Y, z) < 1/2 for every t ≥ 0 and Y ∈ E. The third component is nonnegative. At viscosity one, its total horizontal mass is less than 10−11. The same conclusions and threshold hold for every positive computable viscosity, with the time and horizontal velocity rescaled as in (21). The force is supported in the union of the horizontal support of V and one fixed small neighborhood of p, times T. All smoothness and uniqueness assertions concern every finite time interval.
